audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Isaac's dim eyes, Rebekah/Jacob deception, blessing language, Jacob/Esau wordplay, trembling, stolen blessing accusation, and Esau's hatred.

verses.restored: When Isaac was old and his eyes were dim from seeing, he called Esau his older son and said to him, My son. He said to him, Here I am.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim...

notes.title: Dim eyes
notes.body: Isaac’s impaired sight sets the stage for misrecognition and deception.

modern.text: When Isaac was old and his eyes were so weak that he could no longer see, he called his older son Esau and said to him, “My son.” “Here I am,” Esau replied.

original.text: וַיְהִי֙ כִּֽי זָקֵ֣ן יִצְחָ֔ק וַתִּכְהֶ֥יןָ עֵינָ֖יו מֵרְאֹ֑ת וַיִּקְרָ֞א אֶת עֵשָׂ֣ו בְּנ֣וֹ הַגָּדֹ֗ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ בְּנִ֔י וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו הִנֵּֽנִי

verses.restored: He said, Look, I am old; I do not know the day of my death.

familiar.text: And he said, Behold now, I am old, I know not the day of my death:

modern.text: “Look,” said Isaac, “I am now old, and I do not know the day of my death.

original.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּה נָ֖א זָקַ֑נְתִּי לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְתִּי י֥וֹם מוֹתִֽי

verses.restored: Now take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, go out to the field, and hunt game for me.

familiar.text: Now therefore take, I pray thee, thy weapons, thy quiver and thy bow...

modern.text: Take your weapons—your quiver and bow—and go out into the field to hunt some game for me.

original.text: וְעַתָּה֙ שָׂא נָ֣א כֵלֶ֔יךָ תֶּלְיְךָ֖ וְקַשְׁתֶּ֑ךָ וְצֵא֙ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה וְצ֥וּדָה לִּ֖י צידה

verses.restored: Make me tasty food, such as I love, and bring it to me so I may eat, that my soul may bless you before I die.

familiar.text: And make me savoury meat, such as I love...

modern.text: Then prepare a tasty dish that I love and bring it to me to eat, so that I may bless you before I die.”

original.text: וַעֲשֵׂה לִ֨י מַטְעַמִּ֜ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָהַ֛בְתִּי וְהָבִ֥יאָה לִּ֖י וְאֹכֵ֑לָה בַּעֲב֛וּר תְּבָרֶכְךָ֥ נַפְשִׁ֖י בְּטֶ֥רֶם אָמֽוּת

familiar.text: And Rebekah heard when Isaac spake to Esau his son...

modern.text: Now Rebekah was listening to what Isaac told his son Esau. So when Esau went into the field to hunt game and bring it back,

notes.title: Listen to my voice
notes.body: Rebekah’s instruction echoes the recurring theme of whose voice is heard and obeyed.

modern.text: Now, my son, listen to my voice and do exactly as I tell you.

original.text: וְעַתָּ֥ה בְנִ֖י שְׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹלִ֑י לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י מְצַוָּ֥ה אֹתָֽךְ

modern.text: Go out to the flock and bring me two choice young goats, so that I can make them into a tasty dish for your father—the kind he loves.

verses.restored: Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, Look, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.

familiar.text: And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man...

modern.text: Jacob answered his mother Rebekah, “Look, my brother Esau is a hairy man, but I am smooth-skinned.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֶל רִבְקָ֖ה אִמּ֑וֹ הֵ֣ן עֵשָׂ֤ו אָחִי֙ אִ֣ישׁ שָׂעִ֔ר וְאָנֹכִ֖י אִ֥ישׁ חָלָֽק

familiar.text: My father peradventure will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver...

notes.title: Like a deceiver
notes.body: Jacob fears exposure and curse more than the moral problem of deception itself.

modern.text: What if my father touches me? Then I would be revealed to him as a deceiver, and I would bring upon myself a curse rather than a blessing.”

original.text: אוּלַ֤י יְמֻשֵּׁ֨נִי֙ אָבִ֔י וְהָיִ֥יתִי בְעֵינָ֖יו כִּמְתַעְתֵּ֑עַ וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י עָלַ֛י קְלָלָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א בְרָכָֽה

verses.restored: His mother said to him, Your curse be on me, my son. Only listen to my voice, and go, take them for me.

familiar.text: And his mother said unto him, Upon me be thy curse, my son...

modern.text: His mother replied, “Your curse be on me, my son. Just obey my voice and go get them for me.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אִמּ֔וֹ עָלַ֥י קִלְלָתְךָ֖ בְּנִ֑י אַ֛ךְ שְׁמַ֥ע בְּקֹלִ֖י וְלֵ֥ךְ קַֽח לִֽי

verses.restored: He went and took them and brought them to his mother, and his mother made tasty food such as his father loved.

familiar.text: And he went, and fetched, and brought them to his mother...

modern.text: So Jacob went and got two goats and brought them to his mother, who made the tasty food his father loved.

original.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ וַיִּקַּ֔ח וַיָּבֵ֖א לְאִמּ֑וֹ וַתַּ֤עַשׂ אִמּוֹ֙ מַטְעַמִּ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָהֵ֥ב אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: Rebekah took the desirable garments of Esau her older son, which were with her in the house, and clothed Jacob her younger son.

familiar.text: And Rebekah took goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau...

modern.text: And Rebekah took the finest clothes in the house that belonged to her older son Esau, and she put them on her younger son Jacob.

original.text: וַתִּקַּ֣ח רִ֠בְקָה אֶת בִּגְדֵ֨י עֵשָׂ֜ו בְּנָ֤הּ הַגָּדֹל֙ הַחֲמֻדֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתָּ֖הּ בַּבָּ֑יִת וַתַּלְבֵּ֥שׁ אֶֽת יַעֲקֹ֖ב בְּנָ֥הּ הַקָּטָֽן

modern.text: Then she handed her son Jacob the tasty food and bread she had made.

familiar.text: And he came unto his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I...

modern.text: So Jacob went to his father and said, “My father.” “Here I am!” he answered. “Which one are you, my son?”

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א אֶל אָבִ֖יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָבִ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הִנֶּ֔נִּי מִ֥י אַתָּ֖ה בְּנִֽי

familiar.text: And Jacob said unto his father, I am Esau thy firstborn...

notes.title: False identity claim
notes.body: Jacob directly claims Esau’s identity and firstborn status.

modern.text: Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Please sit up and eat some of my game, so that you may bless me.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶל אָבִ֗יו אָנֹכִי֙ עֵשָׂ֣ו בְּכֹרֶ֔ךָ עָשִׂ֕יתִי כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ אֵלָ֑י קֽוּם נָ֣א שְׁבָ֗ה וְאָכְלָה֙ מִצֵּידִ֔י בַּעֲב֖וּר תְּבָרֲכַ֥נִּי נַפְשֶֽׁךָ

familiar.text: And Isaac said unto his son, How is it that thou hast found it so quickly...

notes.title: Divine name used in deception
notes.body: Jacob invokes the Eternal inside the deception, heightening the moral tension.

modern.text: But Isaac asked his son, “How did you ever find it so quickly, my son?” “Because the LORD your God brought it to me,” he replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִצְחָק֙ אֶל בְּנ֔וֹ מַה זֶּ֛ה מִהַ֥רְתָּ לִמְצֹ֖א בְּנִ֑י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י הִקְרָ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לְפָנָֽי

modern.text: Then Isaac said to Jacob, “Please come closer so I can touch you, my son. Are you really my son Esau, or not?”

notes.body: Isaac perceives contradiction between sound and touch.

modern.text: So Jacob came close to his father Isaac, who touched him and said, “The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”

original.text: וַיִּגַּ֧שׁ יַעֲקֹ֛ב אֶל יִצְחָ֥ק אָבִ֖יו וַיְמֻשֵּׁ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הַקֹּל֙ ק֣וֹל יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְהַיָּדַ֖יִם יְדֵ֥י עֵשָֽׂו

familiar.text: And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy...

modern.text: Isaac did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like those of his brother Esau; so he blessed him.

original.text: וְלֹ֣א הִכִּיר֔וֹ כִּֽי הָי֣וּ יָדָ֗יו כִּידֵ֛י עֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִ֖יו שְׂעִרֹ֑ת וַֽיְבָרְכֵֽהוּ

verses.restored: He said, Are you truly my son Esau? He said, I am.

familiar.text: And he said, Art thou my very son Esau? And he said, I am.

modern.text: Again he asked, “Are you really my son Esau?” And he replied, “I am.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הַגִּ֤שָׁה לִּי֙ וְאֹֽכְלָה֙ מִצֵּ֣יד בְּנִ֔י לְמַ֥עַן תְּבָֽרֶכְךָ֖ נַפְשִׁ֑י וַיַּגֶּשׁ לוֹ֙ וַיֹּאכַ֔ל וַיָּ֧בֵא ל֦וֹ יַ֖יִן וַיֵּֽשְׁתְּ

verses.restored: May the Divine give you from the dew of the heavens and from the fatness of the earth, and abundance of grain and new wine.

notes.body: This blessing echoes the prenatal oracle: the older shall serve the younger.

modern.text: May peoples serve you and nations bow down to you. May you be the master of your brothers, and may the sons of your mother bow down to you. May those who curse you be cursed, and those who bless you be blessed.” Esau’s Lost Hope

familiar.text: And he also had made savoury meat, and brought it unto his father...

modern.text: He too made some tasty food, brought it to his father, and said to him, “My father, sit up and eat of your son’s game, so that you may bless me.”

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ גַּם הוּא֙ מַטְעַמִּ֔ים וַיָּבֵ֖א לְאָבִ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְאָבִ֗יו יָקֻ֤ם אָבִי֙ וְיֹאכַל֙ מִצֵּ֣יד בְּנ֔וֹ בַּעֲב֖וּר תְּבָרֲכַ֥נִּי נַפְשֶֽׁךָ

verses.restored: Isaac his father said to him, Who are you? He said, I am your son, your firstborn, Esau.

familiar.text: And Isaac his father said unto him, Who art thou? And he said, I am thy son...

modern.text: But his father Isaac replied, “Who are you?” “I am Esau, your firstborn son,” he answered.

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֛וֹ יִצְחָ֥ק אָבִ֖יו מִי אָ֑תָּה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֲנִ֛י בִּנְךָ֥ בְכֹֽרְךָ֖ עֵשָֽׂו

verses.restored: Isaac trembled with a very great trembling and said, Who then was he who hunted game and brought it to me? I ate from all before you came, and I blessed him. Yes, blessed he shall be.

familiar.text: And Isaac trembled very exceedingly, and said, Who? where is he...

notes.title: Very great trembling
notes.body: The Hebrew intensifies Isaac’s shock. Yet he does not revoke the blessing.

modern.text: Isaac began to tremble violently and said, “Who was it, then, who hunted the game and brought it to me? Before you came in, I ate it all and blessed him—and indeed, he will be blessed!”

original.text: וַיֶּחֱרַ֨ד יִצְחָ֣ק חֲרָדָה֮ גְּדֹלָ֣ה עַד מְאֹד֒ וַיֹּ֡אמֶר מִֽי אֵפ֡וֹא ה֣וּא הַצָּֽד צַיִד֩ וַיָּ֨בֵא לִ֜י וָאֹכַ֥ל מִכֹּ֛ל בְּטֶ֥רֶם תָּב֖וֹא וָאֲבָרֲכֵ֑הוּ גַּם בָּר֖וּךְ יִהְיֶֽה

verses.restored: When Esau heard his father’s words, he cried out with a great and very bitter cry and said to his father, Bless me, me also, my father!

familiar.text: And when Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry...

modern.text: When Esau heard his father’s words, he let out a loud and bitter cry and said to his father, “Bless me too, O my father!”

original.text: כִּשְׁמֹ֤עַ עֵשָׂו֙ אֶת דִּבְרֵ֣י אָבִ֔יו וַיִּצְעַ֣ק צְעָקָ֔ה גְּדֹלָ֥ה וּמָרָ֖ה עַד מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְאָבִ֔יו בָּרֲכֵ֥נִי גַם אָ֖נִי אָבִֽי

verses.restored: He said, Your brother came with deceit and took your blessing.

familiar.text: And he said, Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing.

modern.text: But Isaac replied, “Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בָּ֥א אָחִ֖יךָ בְּמִרְמָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֖ח בִּרְכָתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: He said, Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has taken my place these two times: he took my birthright, and look, now he has taken my blessing. He said, Have you not reserved a blessing for me?

familiar.text: And he said, Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me...

notes.title: Jacob wordplay
notes.body: Esau links Jacob’s name with taking the heel/supplanting.

modern.text: So Esau declared, “Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has cheated me twice. He took my birthright, and now he has taken my blessing.” Then he asked, “Haven’t you saved a blessing for me?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר הֲכִי֩ קָרָ֨א שְׁמ֜וֹ יַעֲקֹ֗ב וַֽיַּעְקְבֵ֨נִי֙ זֶ֣ה פַעֲמַ֔יִם אֶת בְּכֹרָתִ֣י לָקָ֔ח וְהִנֵּ֥ה עַתָּ֖ה לָקַ֣ח בִּרְכָתִ֑י וַיֹּאמַ֕ר הֲלֹא אָצַ֥לְתָּ לִּ֖י בְּרָכָֽה

verses.restored: Isaac answered and said to Esau, Look, I have made him master over you, and all his brothers I have given to him as servants. With grain and new wine I have sustained him. What then can I do for you, my son?

familiar.text: And Isaac answered and said unto Esau, Behold, I have made him thy lord...

modern.text: But Isaac answered Esau: “Look, I have made him your master and given him all his relatives as servants; I have sustained him with grain and new wine. What is left that I can do for you, my son?”

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַן יִצְחָ֜ק וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְעֵשָׂ֗ו הֵ֣ן גְּבִ֞יר שַׂמְתִּ֥יו לָךְ֙ וְאֶת כָּל אֶחָ֗יו נָתַ֤תִּי לוֹ֙ לַעֲבָדִ֔ים וְדָגָ֥ן וְתִירֹ֖שׁ סְמַכְתִּ֑יו וּלְכָ֣ה אֵפ֔וֹא מָ֥ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֖ה בְּנִֽי

verses.restored: Esau said to his father, Have you only one blessing, my father? Bless me, me also, my father. And Esau lifted his voice and wept.

familiar.text: And Esau said unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father?...

modern.text: Esau said to his father, “Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me too, O my father!” Then Esau wept aloud.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר עֵשָׂ֜ו אֶל אָבִ֗יו הַֽבְרָכָ֨ה אַחַ֤ת הִֽוא לְךָ֙ אָבִ֔י בָּרֲכֵ֥נִי גַם אָ֖נִי אָבִ֑י וַיִּשָּׂ֥א עֵשָׂ֛ו קֹל֖וֹ וַיֵּֽבְךְּ

verses.restored: Isaac his father answered and said to him, Look, away from the fatness of the earth shall your dwelling be, and away from the dew of the heavens above.

familiar.text: And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth...

notes.title: Away from / of
notes.body: The Hebrew preposition can be read as from/of. Context contrasts Esau’s blessing with Jacob’s.

modern.text: His father Isaac answered him: “Behold, your dwelling place shall be away from the richness of the land, away from the dew of heaven above.

original.text: וַיַּ֛עַן יִצְחָ֥ק אָבִ֖יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֑יו הִנֵּ֞ה מִשְׁמַנֵּ֤י הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה מֽוֹשָׁבֶ֔ךָ וּמִטַּ֥ל הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם מֵעָֽל

verses.restored: By your sword you shall live, and your brother you shall serve. But when you grow restless, you shall break his yoke from your neck.

familiar.text: And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother...

modern.text: You shall live by the sword and serve your brother. But when you rebel, you will tear his yoke from your neck.”

original.text: וְעַל חַרְבְּךָ֣ תִֽחְיֶ֔ה וְאֶת אָחִ֖יךָ תַּעֲבֹ֑ד וְהָיָה֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר תָּרִ֔יד וּפָרַקְתָּ֥ עֻלּ֖וֹ מֵעַ֥ל צַוָּארֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him. Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are near; then I will kill Jacob my brother.

familiar.text: And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him...

modern.text: Esau held a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing his father had given him. And Esau said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then I will kill my brother Jacob.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׂטֹ֤ם עֵשָׂו֙ אֶֽת יַעֲקֹ֔ב עַל הַ֨בְּרָכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּרֲכ֖וֹ אָבִ֑יו וַיֹּ֨אמֶר עֵשָׂ֜ו בְּלִבּ֗וֹ יִקְרְבוּ֙ יְמֵי֙ אֵ֣בֶל אָבִ֔י וְאַֽהַרְגָ֖ה אֶת יַעֲקֹ֥ב אָחִֽי

verses.restored: The words of Esau her older son were told to Rebekah. She sent and called Jacob her younger son and said to him, Look, Esau your brother is comforting himself concerning you by planning to kill you.

familiar.text: And these words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah...

modern.text: When the words of her older son Esau were relayed to Rebekah, she sent for her younger son Jacob and told him, “Look, your brother Esau is consoling himself by plotting to kill you.

original.text: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְרִבְקָ֔ה אֶת דִּבְרֵ֥י עֵשָׂ֖ו בְּנָ֣הּ הַגָּדֹ֑ל וַתִּשְׁלַ֞ח וַתִּקְרָ֤א לְיַעֲקֹב֙ בְּנָ֣הּ הַקָּטָ֔ן וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו הִנֵּה֙ עֵשָׂ֣ו אָחִ֔יךָ מִתְנַחֵ֥ם לְךָ֖ לְהָרְגֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Now, my son, listen to my voice. Rise, flee to Laban my brother in Haran.

familiar.text: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice; and arise, flee thou to Laban...

modern.text: So now, my son, obey my voice and flee at once to my brother Laban in Haran.

original.text: וְעַתָּ֥ה בְנִ֖י שְׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹלִ֑י וְק֧וּם בְּרַח לְךָ֛ אֶל לָבָ֥ן אָחִ֖י חָרָֽנָה

verses.restored: Stay with him a few days, until your brother’s heat turns away,

familiar.text: And tarry with him a few days, until thy brother's fury turn away;

modern.text: Stay with him for a while, until your brother’s fury subsides—

original.text: וְיָשַׁבְתָּ֥ עִמּ֖וֹ יָמִ֣ים אֲחָדִ֑ים עַ֥ד אֲשֶׁר תָּשׁ֖וּב חֲמַ֥ת אָחִֽיךָ

verses.restored: until your brother’s anger turns away from you and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send and take you from there. Why should I be bereaved of both of you in one day?

familiar.text: Until thy brother's anger turn away from thee, and he forget that which thou hast done...

modern.text: until your brother’s rage against you wanes and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send for you and bring you back from there. Why should I lose both of you in one day?”

original.text: עַד שׁ֨וּב אַף אָחִ֜יךָ מִמְּךָ֗ וְשָׁכַח֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ וְשָׁלַחְתִּ֖י וּלְקַחְתִּ֣יךָ מִשָּׁ֑ם לָמָ֥ה אֶשְׁכַּ֛ל גַּם שְׁנֵיכֶ֖ם י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד

verses.restored: Rebekah said to Isaac, I am disgusted with my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a woman from the daughters of Heth like these, from the daughters of the land, why should I live?

familiar.text: And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth...

notes.title: Marriage pretext
notes.body: Rebekah frames Jacob’s departure around marriage, while the immediate danger is Esau’s anger.

modern.text: Then Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of these Hittite women. If Jacob takes a Hittite wife from among them, what good is my life?”

original.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רִבְקָה֙ אֶל יִצְחָ֔ק קַ֣צְתִּי בְחַיַּ֔י מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנ֣וֹת חֵ֑ת אִם לֹקֵ֣חַ יַ֠עֲקֹב אִשָּׁ֨ה מִבְּנֽוֹת חֵ֤ת כָּאֵ֨לֶּה֙ מִבְּנ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ לָ֥מָּה לִּ֖י חַיִּֽים
